idiom_name: select over a channel with a time.Ticker/time.After case and a context deadline
implementation_notes: Go has no polling-consumer type and needs none for in-process channels: a receive blocks, so the pull loop collapses into select with a receive case, a time.Ticker/time.After case that implements the idle tick and the bounded wait, a default case when the non-blocking receiveNoWait behaviour is wanted, and a context deadline or cancellation case so a blocked consumer exits on shutdown. The hand-written poll loop stays justified for pull-based brokers and rate-limited APIs, where the client only offers ReadMessage(ctx)/fetch calls and the batch bound and backoff remain application policy.
pitfalls: select with a default case is a non-blocking receive; looping on it without a ticker or backoff is a hot spin, and calling time.After inside the loop allocates a fresh timer every iteration.
A nil channel blocks forever in select, so an unwired channel looks like a silent stall instead of an error - validate the wiring at construction time.
